messages.B 系列采用 1975 年完整多项式，基准雷诺数 2×10^6。适用范围：2–7:
The Wageningen B-series uses the complete 1975 polynomials at a baseline Reynolds number of 2×10^6. Valid ranges: 2–7 blades, expanded area ratio 0.30–1.05, pitch ratio 0.50–1.40 and J=0–1.5.
Choose the baseline mode or the Reynolds number correction from Table 6 of the paper (2×10^6–2×10^9). Enter the Reynolds number at 0.75R. This value applies to the entire curve; for example, enter 20 for 2×10^7. Baseline mode applies no correction; correction mode retains the fit residual at the lower limit.
No corrections for roughness, cavitation, blade thickness variations or behind-hull operation are applied.
messages.在给定直径、转速和螺距范围内进行 B 系列初选。各航速独立选桨，曲线表示设计包络: Preliminary B-series selection searches within the specified diameter, shaft speed and pitch limits. Each ship speed is evaluated independently; the curves show the design envelope. Loads and main engine power are totals for all propellers. Without a diameter limit, the search extends to 25 m; check installation clearance. Matching is limited to the speeds covered by the table.
messages.图谱 1–4 使用 B 系列多项式，基准 Re=2×10^6，要求 i2 = 1: Diagrams 1–4 use the B-series polynomials at the baseline Re=2×10^6 and require i2 = 1. Thrust, torque and main engine power are totals for all propellers. Wake fraction w, thrust deduction fraction t and relative rotative efficiency ηR are taken from the inputs. ηR is the ratio of open-water torque to behind-hull torque at equal thrust. Va=(1-w)Vs, Te=(1-t)Nρn²D⁴KT, Pe=2πNρn³D⁵KQ/(ηRηsηg). The 25 operating points span 0.70–1.30 times the reference J and 0.55–1.15 times the rated shaft speed. Loads outside the propulsion range are for reference only.

messages.螺旋桨优化程序 (POP.1.5)\nM. G. Parsons，1994年12:
Propeller Optimization Program (POP.1.5)
M. G. Parsons, December 1994
1. Method:
1.1    This program implements the Wageningen B-series propeller regression equations proposed by Oosterveld and van Oossanen [1]. Users can either evaluate a given propeller or use Parsons' [2] mathematical programming method to obtain the optimal open-water efficiency for a given application.
1.2   In optimization mode, the user specifies the required thrust and advance speed. The program then uses the Nelder-Mead simplex search method combined with an external penalty function [2] to determine the optimal propeller. Wageningen B-series propellers with 3 to 7 blades are available, including Reynolds number corrections. Optimization across blade counts must be handled by running separately for each count and comparing results. For controllable reversible pitch (CRP) propellers, the program reduces the B-series open-water efficiency by 2%. The program includes Burrill's 5% or 10% back cavitation criteria [3]. The independent optimization variables are the expanded area ratio Ae/Ao, the pitch-diameter ratio P/Dp, and the propeller diameter Dp. The thrust required (within approx. 1 lbf) is determined at each step of the internal search loop. Thus, RPM is not a fourth independent variable but is determined by the equality constraint that generated thrust must equal required thrust. This is an implicit constraint, so the required RPM is found iteratively. Variable constraints are as follows:
__3 <= Nblade <= 7;
0.3 <=  Ae/Ao <= 1.05;
0.5 <=  P/Dp  <= 1.40;
Dpmin <= Dp   <= Dpmax;
0.0  <=   J   <= 1.60;
1 <= Thrust loading <= 2 - per Burrill 5% or 10% limits.

1.4 The optimization objective is to maximize the propeller's open-water efficiency while producing the required thrust at the specified advance speed. The Burrill 5% back cavitation criterion is recommended. The program does not check if the final design is "slightly to the left" of the peak of the efficiency vs. J curve, which is often recommended as a margin against deviation from the predicted operating point RPM. The user should check this on the graphical output.
1.5 If the calculation determines that the RPM required to produce the desired thrust does not converge within 400 iterations, an error message is printed.
1.6 Propeller type allows selection of fixed-pitch or controllable-pitch propellers. Currently, only the Wageningen B-Screw Series is supported, and open-water efficiency is reduced by 2% for the controllable-pitch option to reflect the larger hub.
1.7 Propeller characteristics obtain the blade count and basic parameters of the propeller. If the optimization option is used, these parameters are initial values used by the search algorithm. If the evaluation option is used, these are the values evaluated by the program.
1.7.1 Nblade: Number of propeller blades, supported 3 to 7.
1.7.2 Ae/Ao: Initial search point or evaluated expanded area ratio.
1.7.3 P/Dp: Initial search point or evaluated pitch-diameter ratio.
1.7.4 Dp: Initial search point or evaluated propeller diameter (m).
1.8 Operating conditions obtain ship speed, wake fraction, and required propeller thrust. It also allows selection of 5% or 10% Burrill cavitation constraints and obtains the shaft centerline submergence depth required to calculate the tip cavitation number.
1.8.1 THR: Required thrust per propeller, in kN, THR = Rt/Zp/(1 - t);
1.8.2 Vk: Ship speed, in knots;
1.8.3 w: Mean longitudinal wake fraction;
1.8.4 HWLM: Depth of shaft centerline below waterline, in meters.
1.9 Water properties allow selection of Freshwater @ 15C, Seawater @ 15C, or user-defined water properties.
1.10 When selecting optimization, the minimum and maximum propeller diameters must be specified. If needed, the user can also enter a specific identifier for this run here.
1.10.1 Dpmin: Minimum propeller diameter, in meters. For fixed-pitch propellers, typically about 25% of Dpmax; for controllable-pitch propellers, about 35% of Dpmax.
1.10.2 Dpmax: Maximum propeller diameter allowed by the hull and meeting required clearance, in meters.
1.11 After the analysis process is complete, the program can generate and plot curves of open-water efficiency, KT, and KQ versus J.
References:
1. Oosterveld, M. W. C., and van Oossanen, P., "Further Computer-Analyzed Data of the Wageningen B-Screw Series," International Shipbuilding Progress, Vol.22, No.251, July, 1975.
2. Parsons, M. G., "Optimization Methods for Use in Computer-Aided Ship Design," Proceedings of the First SNAME STAR Symposium, 1975.
3. Comstock, J.P. (ed.), "Principles of Naval Architecture," Vol. II, 1988 Edition, SNAME, New York, p. 182.

messages.湿表面积 S=0 时使用 Holtrop 公式估算；AT 为艉封板浸水面积，AB: S=0 requests the Holtrop wetted-area estimate. AT is immersed transom area; ABT is immersed bulb cross-sectional area at the forward perpendicular; hb is its centroid height above baseline.

messages.van Oortmerssen；独立可选分支包括 Ridgeley–Nevitt: van Oortmerssen; separately selectable branches include Ridgeley–Nevitt (1967) and UBC (1993).

messages.各滑行与预滑行方法具有不同的船底形状、航速和几何要求；有效航速点不足时程序不生成: Planing and pre-planing methods have different bottom-form, speed and geometry requirements. The program rejects a complete curve when too few valid speed points remain. A domain for one method does not validate another.
messages.可选方法包括 Sedov–Perelmootre、Savitsky (1964): Selectable methods include Sedov–Perelmootre, Savitsky (1964), Savitsky–Mercier, Clement–Poup, Clement–Blount, Bunkov, Compton, Wolfson, Radojcic and Almeter; see the active method.
messages.轴系效率和齿轮箱效率分别描述轴系与传动损失；原表为典型参考值，应优先采用设备资料: Shaft and gearbox efficiencies describe separate transmission losses. Legacy tables are typical reference values; prefer equipment data.
messages.推力、转矩、功率与效率按所选推进工况给出；不同图谱不能仅凭相同列名互换。: Thrust, torque, power and efficiency follow the selected operating condition; identical column names do not make different diagrams interchangeable.
messages.FreeShip Plus 螺旋桨计算模块及其原求解器；方法名称以所选图谱为准。: FreeShip Plus propulsion modules and their original solvers; identify the method from the selected diagram.
messages.初选限于指定直径、转速和螺距范围；不保证范围外最优解。匹配不外推，未做空泡、强度: Preliminary design is limited to the specified diameter, RPM and pitch ranges; it does not guarantee an optimum outside them. Matching does not extrapolate. Cavitation, strength, full-scale and regulatory checks are not performed.
messages.所有螺旋桨载荷和主机功率合计；ηR=Q0/Q，旧 i2 只接受 1。未给定直径限: Propeller loads and engine power are totals for all propellers; ηR=Q0/Q and legacy i2 accepts only 1. Without a diameter limit the search extends to 25 m; check installation clearance.
messages.每个航速单独选桨；曲线是设计包络，不是同一支桨的运行曲线。: A propeller is selected independently at each speed; the curve is a design envelope, not the operating curve of one propeller.
messages.M. W. C. Oosterveld & P. van Oossanen, F: M. W. C. Oosterveld & P. van Oossanen, Further Computer-Analyzed Data of Wageningen B-Screw Series, ISP 22(251), July 1975; NMSB Report 479.
messages.内置图谱限于图谱 1–4，基准 Re=2×10^6；未包含粗糙度、空泡、强度和实: Native diagrams are limited to diagrams 1–4 with reference Re=2×10^6; roughness, cavitation, strength and full-scale certification are not included.
messages.伴流比 w、推力减额 t 和相对旋转效率 ηR 保持输入值；ηR 为敞水转矩与船: Wake fraction w, thrust deduction t and relative rotative efficiency ηR remain at their input values. ηR is open-water torque divided by behind-hull torque; legacy i2 accepts only 1.
messages.总有效推力 Te=(1−t)Nρn²D⁴KT；主机功率 Pe=2πNρn³D⁵K: Total effective thrust Te=(1−t)Nρn²D⁴KT; engine power Pe=2πNρn³D⁵KQ/(ηRηsηg). Signed loads outside the propulsion region are not usable engine operating points.
messages.原 POP.1.5 说明提供 3–7 叶 Wageningen B 系列回归与雷: The original POP.1.5 documentation describes 3–7-bladed Wageningen B-series regression with Reynolds correction and optional Burrill 5% or 10% back-cavitation criteria. This is distinct from the newer native preliminary-design workflow.
messages.M. G. Parsons, Propeller Optimization Pr: M. G. Parsons, Propeller Optimization Program POP.1.5, December 1994; Wageningen B-series regression by Oosterveld and van Oossanen.
messages.旧方法说明：3≤桨叶数≤7，0.30≤Ae/Ao≤1.05，0.50≤P/D≤1: Legacy method documentation: 3≤blade count≤7, 0.30≤Ae/Ao≤1.05, 0.50≤P/D≤1.40, 0≤J≤1.6. The native B-series limits are listed separately and must not be mixed with the legacy mode.
messages.内置 B 系列：2–7 叶，Ae/Ao=0.30–1.05，P/D=0.50–1: Native B-series: 2–7 blades, Ae/Ao=0.30–1.05, P/D=0.50–1.40, J=0–1.5. Optional Table 6 Reynolds correction covers 2×10^6–2×10^9. Roughness, cavitation, blade-thickness variation and behind-hull corrections are not applied.
messages.雷诺数输入为 0.75R 处的值，单位为百万；输入 20 表示 2×10^7，整: The Reynolds input is the value at 0.75R in millions: 20 means 2×10^7 and is held constant along the curve.
messages.输出 KT、KQ、敞水效率及零推力、零转矩特征；基准模式的雷诺数为 2×10^6: Outputs include KT, KQ, open-water efficiency and zero-thrust/zero-torque characteristics. Baseline mode uses Reynolds number 2×10^6.
messages.SLOA：总长；B：船宽；AL：侧向受风投影面积；AS：上层建筑侧向投影面积；A: SLOA: overall length; B: beam; AL: lateral projected wind area; AS: lateral projected superstructure area; AT: transverse projected wind area.
messages.S 为侧向投影周长，不含水线及细长构件；C 为船首至侧向投影形心的距离。: S is the perimeter of the lateral projection, excluding the waterline and slender bodies; C is the distance from the bow to its centroid.
messages.SLOA：船体总长，用作艏摇力矩的参考长度。: SLOA: overall length, also the reference length for yaw moment.
messages.AL：船体水线上方的侧向受风投影面积，不是横向面积。: AL: lateral projected wind area above the waterline, not transverse area.
messages.AS：上层建筑的侧向投影面积，不是横向面积。: AS: lateral projected area of the superstructure, not transverse area.
messages.AT：迎艏／迎艉方向的横向受风投影面积；当前力与力矩以此面积归一化。: AT: transverse projected wind area viewed from bow/stern; used to normalize the displayed forces and moment.
messages.S：侧向投影轮廓周长，不含水线段和细长构件。: S: perimeter of the lateral projection, excluding the waterline and slender bodies.
messages.C：从船首量至侧向受风投影面积形心的纵向距离。: C: longitudinal distance from the bow to the centroid of lateral projected wind area.
messages.Vs：船速，与风速一起用于求相对风速和相对风角；单位 m/s。: Vs: vessel speed, combined with wind speed to obtain relative wind speed and angle; unit m/s.
messages.输入风速；程序与船速进行矢量合成，得到相对风速。: Input wind speed; combined vectorially with vessel speed to obtain relative wind speed.
messages.输入风向角；0°时与船速方向作同向标量相加，90°时产生横向分量。: Input wind direction angle; at 0° wind and vessel speed add along one axis, while 90° adds a lateral component.
messages.TF、TA 为首尾吃水；LCG 从船中起以 %LWL 表示，向艏为正；舵作用点: TF and TA are forward and aft drafts. LCG is %LWL from amidships, positive forward; rudder force center XR is %LWL from amidships, positive aft.
messages.GYRAD 为艏摇回转半径与 LWL 的比值；AR=舵面积/(LWL·T)；H/: GYRAD is yaw radius of gyration divided by LWL; AR=rudder area/(LWL·T); H/T is depth/draft ratio, with 1000 representing deep water in the inherited help.
messages.线性评估给出 Nomoto 时间常数与增益、Clarke 回转指标、裸船体动稳定: Linear evaluation gives Nomoto time constants/gains, Clarke turning index, bare-hull dynamic stability and phase margin. The inherited help uses nondimensional outputs except phase margin in °.
messages.回转预估给出稳定回转直径、战术直径、进距、横距和回转中稳定航速。: Turning prediction gives steady turning diameter, tactical diameter, advance, transfer and steady turning speed.
messages.M. G. Parsons, MPP-1.3, December 1994；Cl: M. G. Parsons, MPP-1.3, December 1994; Clarke, Gedling & Hine (RINA 124, 1982); Lyster & Knights (NECIES 1978–1979); Fugino (Michigan NAME Report 184, 1976); Inoue, Hirano & Kijima (ISP 28(321), 1981).
messages.LWL：水线长度，为几何和无量纲导数的参考长度。: LWL: waterline length, used as the reference length for geometry and nondimensional derivatives.
messages.B：水线处最大船宽。: B: maximum beam at the waterline.
messages.CB：以 LWL 为长度基准的方形系数。: CB: block coefficient based on LWL.
messages.LCG：从船中起算的重心纵向位置，以 %LWL 表示，向艏为正。: LCG: longitudinal center of gravity in %LWL from amidships, positive forward.
messages.XR：舵作用点从船中起算的纵向位置，以 %LWL 表示，向艉为正，通常取舵前缘后: XR: longitudinal rudder force-center position in %LWL from amidships, positive aft, typically at the quarter-chord point.
messages.VK：初始或参考船速，单位 kn。: VK: initial or reference vessel speed, unit kn.
messages.参与操纵性计算的水密度，单位 kg/m³。: Water density used in the maneuvering calculation, unit kg/m³.
messages.运动黏度以 10⁻⁶ m²/s 为输入单位；1.61 表示 1.61×10⁻⁶: Kinematic viscosity is entered in 10⁻⁶ m²/s; 1.61 means 1.61×10⁻⁶ m²/s.
messages.GYRAD：艏摇回转半径 k33 与 LWL 的比值；原说明默认0.25。: GYRAD: yaw radius of gyration k33 divided by LWL; the inherited default is 0.25.
messages.H/T：水深与船舶吃水之比；原说明用1000表示深水。线性浅水修正低于1.3不可: H/T: water depth divided by vessel draft; 1000 represents deep water in the inherited help. Linear shallow-water correction is unreliable below 1.3.
messages.TE：舵机时间常数，单位 s；原说明默认2.5。: TE: steering-engine time constant in s; the inherited default is 2.5.
messages.AR：舵总面积除以 LWL×T。: AR: total rudder area divided by LWL×T.
messages.AB：艏部与垂直艏的浸没中纵剖面积差除以 LWL×T；艏垂线前凸出为正，后切为负: AB: difference from a plumb bow in submerged centerplane profile area divided by LWL×T; forward protrusion is positive and cutaway is negative.
messages.推进布置选择：0、1或2；该值也影响回转预估的单桨／双桨分支。: Propulsion arrangement selector: 0, 1 or 2; also selects the single-/twin-screw turning-prediction branch.
messages.单桨船艉型：0为封闭艉，1为敞开艉。: Single-screw stern type: 0 for closed stern, 1 for open stern.
messages.舵数量；双桨船应指定单舵或双舵。: Number of rudders; specify one or two for a twin-screw vessel.
messages.用于回转预估的舵角，单位 °。: Rudder angle used for turning prediction, unit °.
messages.按线性导数评估航向稳定性与操纵性。: Evaluate course stability and maneuverability using linear derivatives.
messages.按独立回归模型预估回转圈特征。: Predict turning-circle characteristics with the separate regression model.
messages.输出线性化运动方程的状态变量形式；同时启用线性评估。: Output the state-variable form of the linearized motion equations; also enables linear evaluation.
messages.主机等效惯性矩采用 kg·m²，须折算至单根桨轴转速；求解器另加桨的自动惯性项，: Equivalent engine inertia is in kg·m² referred to a single propeller shaft. The solver adds its own propeller-inertia term; do not enter it again. Multiply t·m² by 1000; refer inertia between shafts using the squared speed ratio.
messages.原柴油机型号、功率、转速与惯性矩表属于输入参考资料，应优先采用实际设备数据。: The inherited diesel-model, power, RPM and inertia table is input reference material; prefer actual equipment data.

messages.Maneuvering Prediction Program (MPP-1.3):
Maneuvering Prediction Program (MPP-1.3)
M. G. Parsons, December, 1994
1. METHODS:
1.1  This program offers two main options: Linear Evaluation which implements the
methods proposed by Clarke, Gedling, and Hine (1) for the  assessment  of  course
stability,  turning  ability,  and  controllability  by  a  helmsman; and Turning
Prediction which  implements  the  multiple linear regression equations presented
by Lyster and Knights (2) for the estimation of turning circle characteristics.
1.2  The  user should consult the Clarke paper prior to using the program. If the
Linear  Evaluation option is used, the user can also obtain the linearized maneu-
vering equations of motion in state variable form (3).
1.3  In the Linear Evaluation option, the linear derivatives are estimated using
the multiple linear regression equations presented by Clarke et al (1). The velo-
city derivatives  were obtained from 72 sets of data from rotating arm and planar
motion  tests.  Acceleration  derivatives  were  obtained from planar motion test
data. The  independent  variables  include  T/LWL, CB*B/T, B/LWL, and B/T. Clarke
feels  that  these  results  are  at  least  as  effective  as the semi-empirical
equations developed by Wagner Smitt, Norrbin, or  Inoue. Water  depth corrections
were added  by  regressing  the  data  presented by Fugino (4) for the Tokyo Maru
( CB = 0.805 ) and the  Mariner ( CB = 0.589 ). Independent  variables  in  these
analyses were CB and inverse powers of F = (H/T) -1. These  can be used for water
depths down to H/T= 1.3, but are considered unreliable below this value. The trim
corrections presented by Inoue (5) are used  for  the  velocity  derivatives. The
independent variable  in  these corrections  is the trim to mean draft ratio. The
various  time  constants  and  gains  in  the  first-  and  second-order Nomoto's
equations are calculated from the linear derivatives.
1.4  The quantities calculated to allow evaluation of the maneuvering performance
of the vessels are as follows:
1.4.1 Inverse time  constant (1/T')  and  inverse  gain  (1/K'). Turning  ability
increases  with  decreasing 1/K' while course stability and quickness of response
to helm increases with 1/T'.
1.4.2 Clarke's turning index P.This quantity is derived from the linear equations
as  the  amount  of  turn achieved in one ship length using a unit step rudder. A
minimum value of 0.3 (equivalent to about 10° for a 35° step rudder,
within the  limits  of  the  linearized  equations of motion) is recommended with
values as low as 0.2 considered acceptable for large tankers.
1.4.3 Bare hull  dynamic  stability  criterion C. This must be positive for open-
loop, controls-fixed course stability of the bare hull.
1.4.4 Phase margin applicable to the closed-loop steering system.The phase margin
of the ship transfer function, including the steering gear, is calculated. Nomoto
notes  that  by  anticipating  the  shipÂs  turning, a typical helmsman can apply
between 20 and 30° of phase advance.  Thus, the  ship  with  steering gear
cannot have more than this amount of negative phase margin  for  the  combination
of the ship and helmsman to be closed-loop stable on course. Thus, a phase margin
greater than about -20° is recommended for reasonable human control.
1.5 All  output  is  nondimensional  following Clarke (1) except the phase margin
which is expressed in degrees.
1.6 In the completely independent Turning Prediction option, the regression equa-
tions developed by Lyster and Knights (2) from sea trial results are used to  es-
timate turning  characteristics for a user-input rudder angle and approach speed.
The  dependence  of the turns of single screw ships on the direction of propeller
rotation and the ratio of the mean draft to the design draft were not implemented.
1.7 The option produces estimates of the following:
- steady turning diameter (meters)
- tactical diameter (meters)
- advance (meters)
- transfer (meters)
- steady speed in the turn (knots)
1.8  This model is for  deep water and includes no dependence on water depth. The
range of the ship parameters included in regression data set is as follows:
+-------------+-------------------+-------------------------+
| Parameter   |   Single screw    |       Twin screw        |
+-------------+-------------------+-------------------------+
|     Lpp     |  54,9 ... 329,2 m |    76,2 ... 225,6 m     |
|     Cb      |  0,56 ... 0,87    |    0,42 ... 0,62        |
|rudder angle |  10,0 ... 45 °.|    10,0 ... 35 °.    |
|     L/B     |  5,56 ... 9,09    |    5,00 ... 16,67       |
|   trim/Lpp  |  0,00 ... 0,05    |   -0,01 ... 0,03        |
|     AR      |  0,01 ... 0,04    | 0,01 ... 0,02 per rudder|
|     AB      | -0,11 ... 0,04    |   -0,10 ... 0,0         |
|     Fr      |  0,06 ... 0,298   |   0,074 ... 0,655       |
+-------------+-------------------+-------------------------+
This model should be used with CAUTION outside this range.
2.   INPUT:
2.1  The input to MPP is through a series as follows:
- LWL length on waterline in meters
- B maximum beam on waterline in meters
- TF draft forward in meters
- TA draft aft in meters
- CB block coefficient on LWL
- LCG longitudinal center of gravity in %LWL from amidships; + forward
- GYRAD yaw radius of gyration k33 as a fraction of LWL; default value 0.25
- AB difference between the submerged bow profile area  on  the  centerplane  and
that of a plumb bow as fraction of LWL*T; i.e.,AB = area forward of STA0/(LWL*T),
positive when a bulbous bow projects forward of  the  forward  perpendicular,  or
AB = cutaway  area  aft  of  STA0/(LWL*T), negative  with a raked stem or cutaway
forefoot.
2.2  Steering Characteristics obtains the rudder area, steering gear  time  cons-
tant, position of the rudder center of effort (typically the 1/4 chord point from
the leading edge), and selection of single or twin screw. The rudder area can  be
input either as a fraction of LWL*T or automatically as the minumum  rudder  area
specified  by  Det  Norske  Veritas for commercial vessels. For single screw, the
sterm  type  must  be  designated  as a closed or open stern. For twin screw, the
number of rudders must be designated as one or two.
2.2.1  AR total rudder  area  as fraction of LWL*T; i.e., AR = A/(LWL*T);  option
is calculated from the Det Norske Veritas minimum rudder area
2.2.2  TE steering gear time constant in seconds; default value is 2.5 s
2.2.3  XR center of effort of rudder in %LWL from amidships;+ aft;i.e.,about 49.0
2.3    Operating Conditions obtains the water depth and the initial vessel speed.
2.3.1  H/T water depth to ship draft ratio (H/T); input 1000 for deep water
2.3.2  VK initial or reference ship speed in knots
3. REFERENCES:
1. Clarke  D., Gedling  P., and Hine  G., "The Application of Manoevring Criteria
in Hull Design Using Linear Theory", Transactions RINA, Vol. 124, 1982.
2. Lyster  C. A., and Knights  H. L., "Prediction  Equations  for  Ships' Turning
Circles", Transactions NECIES 1978-1979.
3. Parsons M. G., "Informal  Notes for NA530 Automatic Control in Naval Architec-
ture  and  Marine  Engineering", Vol. I, "Classical Control," and Vol. II "Modern
Control."
4. Fugino  M., "Maneuverability in Restricted Waters: State of the Art", The Uni-
versity of Michigan NAME Report No. 184, Aug., 1976.
5. Inoue, S., Hirano, M., and Kijima, K., "Hydrodynamic Derivatives on Ship Mano-
evring", International Shipbuilding Progress, Vol. 28, No. 321, 1981.
